14485	def _compare_outputs(ref_path: Path, candidate_path: Path,
14486	                     dtype: str) -> Tuple[str, float]:
14487	    """Compare two .npy tensors. Returns (status, max_relative_error).
14488	
14489	    status is one of "ok" | "numerical_fail" | "deterministic". The
14490	    "deterministic" tag is set only when the two arrays are bit-identical
14491	    (np.array_equal). Strict-mode 3x re-run determinism is checked
14492	    separately by _check_determinism_3x.
14493	    """

14497	    b = np.load(candidate_path)
14498	    if a.shape != b.shape:
14499	        return ("numerical_fail", float("inf"))
14500	    diff = np.abs(a.astype(np.float64) - b.astype(np.float64))
14501	    rel = diff / (np.abs(a).astype(np.float64) + atol)
14502	    max_rel = float(rel.max()) if rel.size else 0.0
14503	    if np.allclose(a, b, rtol=rtol, atol=atol, equal_nan=False):
14504	        if np.array_equal(a, b):
14505	            return ("deterministic", max_rel)
14506	        return ("ok", max_rel)

15284	    # safe, else None (⇒ full build). The plan splits the variant's TUs into
15285	    # the affected set (recompiled WITH the changed macros) and the reused set
15286	    # (the AOT objects, byte-identical because their command is unchanged).
15287	    def _plan_incremental_build(spec, variant_sources, host_extra, device_extra,
15288	                                report) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
15289	        import re as _re
15290	        vendor = get_arch_entry(spec.arch).vendor
15291	        # Object layout we can reason about: cpu/cuda/hip TUs compile to one
15292	        # <stem>.o per source under the AOT build dir. Pallas has no objects.
15293	        if vendor not in ("cpu", "cuda", "hip"):
15294	            return None
15295	        # The AOT build the variant derives from. If variant_sources were
15296	        # REPLACED (emitter/synth/polyhedral emitted a fresh file), object
15297	        # reuse is unsafe — fall back.
15298	        try:
15299	            aot_sources = _resolve_sources(spec)
15300	        except Exception:
15301	            return None
15302	        aot_stems = {Path(s).stem for s in aot_sources}
15303	        v_stems = {Path(s).stem for s in variant_sources}
15304	        if v_stems != aot_stems:
15305	            report.write("    [incremental] variant sources differ from AOT "
15306	                         "(emitter/synth/polyhedral) — full build.\n")
15307	            return None
15308	        # Changed macros = the SG_TUNED_* -D tokens this variant ADDS on top of
15309	        # the base build. A NON-macro flag delta (maxrregcount, fast-math, etc.)
15310	        # affects EVERY TU, so any such token forces a full build.
15311	        macro_re = _re.compile(r"^-D(SG_TUNED_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)=")
15312	        changed_macros: set = set()
15313	        for f in list(host_extra) + list(device_extra):
15314	            m = macro_re.match(f)
15315	            if m:
15316	                changed_macros.add(m.group(1))
15317	            elif f.startswith("-D") or f.startswith("-"):
15318	                # A non-SG_TUNED flag addition (e.g. --maxrregcount, a fast-math
15319	                # token, a -D the macro map doesn't own) touches all TUs.
15320	                if not f.startswith("-DSG_TUNED_"):
15321	                    report.write("    [incremental] non-macro variant flag "
15322	                                 "%r touches all TUs — full build.\n" % f)
15323	                    return None
15324	        if not changed_macros:
15325	            return None  # nothing macro-specific to be incremental about
15326	        # Map each changed macro to the TU(s) whose PREPROCESSED INPUT reads it.
15327	        # A changed SG_TUNED_* macro affects a TU's object iff the macro token
15328	        # appears anywhere in {TU body ∪ its transitive #include closure} — a
15329	        # header-defined macro IS read by a TU that (transitively) #includes the
15330	        # header, but is NOT read by a sibling TU whose own closure never reaches
15331	        # that header. We compute each TU's closure with the same mtime-memoized
15332	        # walker _hash_sources uses, so the attribution is exact and matches the
15333	        # freshness hash. This is a strict superset of the old body-only check
15334	        # (closure ⊇ body) and is the single-cell-source-scoping lever: e.g. a
15335	        # decoder-exclusive macro (SG_TUNED_DEC_GEMM_INTERLEAVE) lives only in the
15336	        # decoder launcher's closure, so the vit/mamba launcher objects are
15337	        # PROVABLY unaffected and their prebuilt AOT .o link in unchanged — the
15338	        # dispatch-table symbols (fused_wired_cells.inc references every model's
15339	        # real launcher) all still resolve because the .o IS linked, just not
15340	        # recompiled. SAFE by construction: a macro absent from a TU's entire
15341	        # preprocessed input cannot change that TU's object.
15342	        exts_tu = {".cu", ".cpp", ".cc", ".cxx", ".hip", ".c"}
15343	        _roots = _include_search_roots()
15344	        affected: set = set()
15345	        # Per-TU read-set of changed macros (body + transitive include closure),
15346	        # via the mtime-memoized _tu_closure_tuned_macros (computed once per TU
15347	        # per sweep, NOT per variant — the per-variant cost is set lookups, not
15348	        # ~90 header reads). A macro found in NO TU's closure is genuinely
15349	        # unattributable (read via a path the include walker can't see) → fall
15350	        # back to a full build.
15351	        _located: set = set()
15352	        for src in variant_sources:
15353	            p = Path(src)
15354	            if p.suffix not in exts_tu:
15355	                continue
15356	            tu_macros = _tu_closure_tuned_macros(p, _roots)
15357	            if tu_macros is None:
15358	                # Unreadable TU/header in the closure — can't prove the plan.
15359	                return None
15360	            hit = {mac for mac in changed_macros if mac in tu_macros}
15361	            if hit:
15362	                affected.add(p)
15363	                _located |= hit
15364	        # If a changed macro is read by NO TU's closure, it is read via a path the
15365	        # include walker cannot attribute (e.g. a compiler-injected or out-of-tree
15366	        # header) — we cannot prove which objects are unchanged, so fall back.
15367	        for mac in changed_macros:
15368	            if mac not in _located:
15369	                report.write("    [incremental] macro %s not located in any TU "
15370	                             "closure (unattributable) — full build.\n" % mac)
15371	                return None
15372	        tu_sources = [Path(s) for s in variant_sources
15373	                      if Path(s).suffix in exts_tu]
15374	        # A PYBIND-module-owning TU (bindings.cpp) bakes PyInit_<TORCH_EXTENSION_
15375	        # NAME> into its object. The variant build uses a DIFFERENT module name
15376	        # (per-config module_suffix) than the AOT base whose object we'd reuse, so
15377	        # a reused PYBIND object exports the WRONG PyInit_ and the variant .so
15378	        # fails to import ("does not define module export function PyInit_<name>")
15379	        # — torch then falls back to a full build, so the incremental attempt is
15380	        # PURE WASTE. Force every PYBIND-owning TU into the recompiled set so its
15381	        # PyInit_ matches the variant module name; the costly sibling-model
15382	        # megakernel objects (the real target of reuse) still link from cache.
15383	        _pyinit_forced = 0
15384	        for p in tu_sources:
15385	            if p not in affected and _tu_emits_pyinit_module(p):
15386	                affected.add(p)
15387	                _pyinit_forced += 1
15388	        if _pyinit_forced:
15389	            report.write("    [incremental] forcing recompile of %d PYBIND-"
15390	                         "module TU(s) (PyInit_ is module-name-specific; a reused "
15391	                         "object would break the variant .so import).\n"
15392	                         % _pyinit_forced)
15393	        unchanged = [p for p in tu_sources if p not in affected]
15394	        # No savings if everything (or nothing) is affected.
15395	        if not affected or not unchanged:
15396	            return None
15397	        # Locate the prebuilt AOT object for each unchanged TU. The AOT build
15398	        # dir mirrors _torch_load's module_name (no variant suffix).
15399	        aot_module = (f"grokking_compiled_{spec.optimizer}_"
15400	                      f"{spec.model}_{spec.arch}")
15401	        aot_build_dir = spec.out_dir / aot_module
15402	        if not aot_build_dir.is_dir():
15403	            report.write("    [incremental] AOT build dir %s absent — full "
15404	                         "build.\n" % aot_build_dir)
15405	            return None
15406	        reuse_objs: List[Path] = []
15407	        for p in unchanged:
15408	            # Mirror torch.utils.cpp_extension's object-naming EXACTLY: a CUDA
15409	            # source (.cu/.cuh) under a with_cuda build compiles to
15410	            # ``<stem>.cuda.o`` (the disambiguation it uses so a foo.cpp and
15411	            # foo.cu don't collide); every other TU compiles to ``<stem>.o``.
15412	            # The old lookup only tried ``<stem>.o``, so it NEVER found the
15413	            # ``.cuda.o`` object for the model launcher TUs (.cu) and silently
15414	            # fell back to a full build — defeating the whole incremental lever.
15415	            # Try the cpp_extension-correct name first, then the bare ``.o`` as a
15416	            # fallback for host TUs / older torch, requiring an exact on-disk hit.
15417	            _is_cuda_tu = p.suffix in (".cu", ".cuh")
15418	            _cands = ([p.stem + ".cuda.o", p.stem + ".o"] if _is_cuda_tu
15419	                      else [p.stem + ".o", p.stem + ".cuda.o"])
15420	            obj = None
15421	            for _cand in _cands:
15422	                _o = aot_build_dir / _cand
15423	                if _o.is_file():
15424	                    obj = _o
15425	                    break
15426	            if obj is None:
15427	                # No prebuilt object under either naming — cannot prove reuse,
15428	                # so fall back to a full build (never reuse on doubt).
15429	                report.write("    [incremental] AOT object for %s missing "
15430	                             "(tried %s) — full build.\n"
15431	                             % (p.name, ", ".join(_cands)))
15432	                return None
15433	            reuse_objs.append(obj)
15434	        report.write("    [incremental] recompiling %d/%d TU(s) carrying %s; "
15435	                     "reusing %d AOT object(s).\n"
15436	                     % (len(affected), len(tu_sources),
15437	                        sorted(changed_macros), len(reuse_objs)))
15438	        return {"affected_sources": [Path(p) for p in affected],
15439	                "reuse_objects": reuse_objs,
15440	                "changed_macros": sorted(changed_macros)}

## 3. Bugs / risks found

### Potential issue A — record-and-replay reloads captured float32 AS the validation dtype (LOW; by design but worth a flag)
`_replay_arg_construction` (14354–14355) and `_capture_real_inputs._to_npy`
(14220–14222) capture tensors as **float32** (`.cpu().float().numpy()`), then
replay reloads them `.to(dtype=dtype)`. For a float16/bf16 production op this
round-trips fp32→fp16, so the replay inputs are NOT bit-identical to what the
real workload fed (which may have been fp16 directly). The docstring acknowledges
"float32 capture preserves the numerical content" (14352–14353). Replay is a
fidelity upgrade gated behind the strict oracle, so this is not a correctness
hole, but the replayed-input oracle/candidate are both fp32-rounded — a flag for
the verification phase, not a HARD-gate violation.

### Potential issue B — `_tc_relevant_device_flags` keeps only 4 tile macros, but `_GEMM_TILE_DIM_NAMES` routes 10 dims to the TC timer (MEDIUM; possible wasted-rebuild / blind-timing edge)
`_GEMM_TILE_DIM_NAMES` (14840–14854) includes `dec_gemm_stages`, `mb_gemm_stages`,
`dec_gemm_interleave`, `mb_gemm_interleave`, `vit_gemm_interleave`, `pipe_depth`
— a config varying any of these triggers `_time_megakernel_tc_step`. But
`_tc_relevant_device_flags` `keep_macros` (14897–14900) is ONLY
`{SG_TUNED_TILE_M, SG_TUNED_TILE_N, SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK,
SG_TUNED_VIT_DW_SPLITK}` — the gemm-stages / interleave / pipe-depth macros are
DROPPED before the TC module is built. Consequence: a config that varies ONLY
`dec_gemm_stages` (etc.) routes to the real-TC timer but builds a TC module whose
flag set is identical to the default (those macros stripped) → the TC binary is
byte-identical and the "real TC" timing is just as blind to that dim as the cheap
timer, while paying a TC JIT build. The comment at 14826–14834 claims these are
"confirmed read by model_stage_*_tc.cuh" yet their macros aren't forwarded.
Either `keep_macros` should include the corresponding `SG_TUNED_*GEMM_STAGES/
*INTERLEAVE/*PIPE_DEPTH` macro spellings, or those dims should not be in
`_GEMM_TILE_DIM_NAMES`. Worth confirming the exact `-D` macro spellings emitted
by `resolve_macros` for those dims during the verification phase. (Cite:
14840–14854 vs 14897–14900.)

### Potential issue C — `_time_megakernel_tc_step` hardcodes AdamW hyperparams for ALL optimizers (LOW–MEDIUM; timing-only)
`_call()` invokes `mod.tc_train_step(... lr,beta1,beta2,eps,wd,bc1,bc2, 1, 0)`
(15022–15029) with fixed `beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98` and the TU is always the
`*_real_adamw_tc.cu` cell (14820–14824). The TC real-step timer therefore times
the AdamW TC step regardless of `spec.optimizer`. Since the tile dims being swept
live in the GEMM/dW substrate (shared across optimizers) and this path is
timing-only (the fp64 parity gate validates the actual production op elsewhere),
the measured tile-dim sensitivity is still representative — but a non-AdamW
optimizer's winner tile config is being chosen on an AdamW TC step. Flag for
verification, not a parity break.

### Potential issue D — `_compare_outputs` "ok" status is allclose at fp32 tol, not the fp64 HARD gate (INFORMATIONAL)
`_compare_outputs` (14485–14507) uses `TOLERANCES[dtype]` (default `1e-3,1e-4`)
and is the **timing-pass** same-dtype oracle, distinct from the production HARD
gate (fp64 parity 1e-4 / SAM 2.5e-2 + A/A/A determinism) which is armed via the
P0-1 `_default_correctness_hook` at 16303–16314 and applied in `pick_winner`.
This is correct by design (doc 14790-onwards) — noting it so the two oracles are
not conflated.
